title: Boeing FY2022 Form 10-K — Note 1 accounting policy: program accounting margin and reach-forward loss mechanics
key_points: The determination of net realizable value of commercial aircraft program costs is based on quarterly program reviews that estimate revenue and cost to be incurred to complete the program accounting quantity.
When estimated costs to complete exceed estimated program revenues to go, a program loss provision (reach-forward loss) is recorded.
For long-term contracts, when the estimate to complete exceeds total estimated contract revenues, a loss provision is recorded.
Program margin is therefore a forward-looking estimate spread across an accounting quantity of units, not a period-matched revenue-minus-cost computation.

When estimated costs to complete exceed estimated program revenues to go, a program loss provision is recorded.

title: Boeing FY2022 Form 10-K — Note 7: 787 reach-forward loss of $3,460M recorded Q4 2021 as reduction to deferred production costs
key_points: During Q4 2021 Boeing determined that estimated costs to complete the 787 program plus costs already included in 787 inventory exceeded estimated revenues from the program.
The resulting reach-forward loss of $3,460M was recorded as a reduction to deferred production costs.

At December 31, 2022 and 2021, 787 program inventory included deferred production costs of $12,689M and $11,693M, supplier advances of $1,831M and $1,907M, and unamortized tooling and other non-recurring costs of $1,722M and $1,815M.

At December 31, 2022, $9,881M of 787 deferred production costs, unamortized tooling and other non-recurring costs are expected to be recovered from units in the accounting quantity with firm orders, and $4,530M from units representing expected future orders.
Boeing expensed 787 abnormal production costs of $1,240M (2022) and $468M (2021).
In April 2022 Boeing decided to pause 777X-9 production during 2022 and 2023, resulting in abnormal production costs expensed as incurred; $325M was expensed in FY2022.
The 777X program has near break-even margins at December 31, 2022.

title: Boeing 2022 10-K — Note 13: Commercial Crew reach-forward loss increase and future loss risk
key_points: During 2022 Boeing increased the Commercial Crew reach-forward loss by $288 million, reflecting higher estimated costs to complete crewed flight tests and revised schedules for the crewed flight test and three post-certification missions.
Post-certification missions are now assumed to be completed by 2026 based on NASA's revised launch plans, versus a prior assumption of 2024.
Boeing states: 'Risk remains that we may record additional losses in future periods.'
At December 31, 2022 Boeing had approximately $180 million of capitalized precontract costs and $159 million of potential termination liabilities to suppliers related to unauthorized future missions.
raw_excerpt: During the year ended December 31, 2022, we increased the reach-forward loss by $288 primarily reflecting increases to estimated costs related to completing the crewed flight tests and revised schedules for both the crewed flight test and three post certification missions... We had previously assumed that the post certification missions would be completed by 2024. Risk remains that we may record additional losses in future periods. At December 31, 2022, we had approximately $180 of capitalized precontract costs and $159 of potential termination liabilities to suppliers related to unauthorized future missions.

title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — Income statement structure, cost of sales as % of revenues, and unallocated items (why gross margin is a weak metric)
url: kb_demo/financebench/pdfs/BOEING_2022_10K.pdf · p28 (cost of sales as % of revenues); p55 (Consolidated Statements of Operations); p62 (segment bridge); p117 (Unallocated items)
key_points: Boeing's income statement presents 'Cost of products' ($53,969M in 2022) against 'Sales of products' ($55,893M) and 'Cost of services' ($9,109M) against 'Sales of services' ($10,715M); there is no gross profit or gross margin line item.
Boeing's own MD&A discusses 'Cost of sales as a % of Revenues' — 94.7% in 2022 vs 95.2% in 2021 vs 109.8% in 2020 — rather than a gross margin metric.
The 10-K's headline consolidated profitability indicators are loss from operations, operating margins, core operating margins, and diluted/core loss per share; gross margin is not among them.

A large block of cost sits outside any gross-margin construct: 'Unallocated items, eliminations and other' was $(1,532)M in 2022, $(1,267)M in 2021, $(2,355)M in 2020, plus the FAS/CAS service cost adjustment of $1,143M / $1,173M / $1,383M.
Unallocated items include share-based plans, deferred compensation, amortization of previously capitalized interest, R&D expense, and eliminations and other unallocated items.

Under program accounting, current-period cost of sales is a function of estimated total program cost spread over a multi-decade accounting quantity (with reach-forward losses and abnormal production costs recognized separately), rather than of cash spent on units delivered in the period.
